title: Book 2 — Euterpe, Chapter 355
paragraphs: Then when the Ethiopian had gone away out of Egypt, the blind man returned from the marshland and began to rule again, having lived for those fifty years on an island he had made by piling up ashes and earth. Whenever any Egyptian visited him bringing food — as each had been appointed to do without the Ethiopian's knowledge — he also bade them bring some ashes as their gift. No one was able to find this island before Amyrtaios; that is, for more than seven hundred years the kings who rose before Amyrtaios were not able to find it. The name of this island is Elbo, and its size is ten furlongs on each side.
